Quality management

Use factory evidence to ask better approval questions.

A useful buyer review connects each declaration, report or certificate to the correct company, site, material, tested construction, intended use and validity period.

  • Confirm whether a file covers the factory, management system, raw material or finished product.
  • Check sample description, test method, date, issuing body and destination-market relevance.
  • Record the approved material, dimensions, artwork, production lot, pack count and shipment checks.

01 · Food-contact documents

Product and intended-use evidence

Available LFGB, DGCCRF and related food-contact reports can support buyer review when the tested paper or finished construction represents the proposed order. Confirm food type, contact conditions, temperature and test scope.

LFGBBfR reviewDGCCRFProduct-specific scope

02 · PFAS evidence

Declarations and testing matched to construction

PFAS-related evidence may include supplier declarations, material statements or product-specific reports. Review analyte scope, method, reporting limits and sample identity before using a commercial claim.

Review PFAS-free options →

03 · Sustainability and paper sourcing

FSC and EUDR are separate workstreams

FSC documentation can support certified sourcing claims for the applicable paper and chain-of-custody route. EUDR requires product-scope analysis and due-diligence data such as origin, species and geolocation; it is not a product certificate.

View FSC PDFReview EUDR Support

04 · Factory and quality management

Site, process and shipment controls

Available BSCI, BRC and ISO-related files support supplier screening. Order-level control should still cover approved materials, dimensions, artwork, production lots, pack counts and shipment preparation.
